target_customer: US healthcare providers, notably behavioral health and clinics, that lose revenue to denials and documentation gaps
problem: Claims are denied because of documentation and coding gaps nobody catches until the payer says no.
business_model: B2B SaaS platform plus billing as a service for providers without CDI or billing teams
product_category: AI revenue integrity and compliance for healthcare

founders.name: Dmitry Karpov
founders.background_notes: No prior employers or education listed on the YC page.

founders.name: Sergey Yudovskiy
founders.background_notes: Described on the YC page as a mathematician.

technical_complexity.rationale: Agents that read EHR and payer screens without APIs plus compliance logic is demanding integration work, but built on commodity LLMs.

defensibility.rationale: UI-level EHR access avoids integration projects but is copyable; many vendors cover coding, CDI, prior auth and appeals separately.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Per Adentris's own comparison page, established vendors already covered each module. No acquisition or copying event was found.

market_need_then: The company cites billions lost to denied claims traced to documentation and coding gaps; it claims a 62 percent denial reduction for customers (company figure).

branding.domain_note: adentris.com is the company domain; WorkDone predecessor used a separate name.

identity.visual_style: Short bold headlines with italic emphasis
identity.voice_and_tone: Direct, outcome and speed focused (Live in 30 days)

rebrands.why: Not stated; coincides with expansion from documentation copilot to full revenue integrity platform

brand_strength.rationale: Invented name with little press or community around it; trade press features listed on its own site.

pivots.to: Adentris AI revenue integrity platform with coding QA, prior authorization, appeals and billing as a service
pivots.why: Expansion across the revenue integrity workflow; a May 2026 release adds five modules.

outcome_analysis: Adentris, formerly WorkDone, raised a 1.8 million dollar pre-seed in April 2025 and joined the Spring 2025 batch. It has broadened into a multi-module platform with named behavioral health customers. It sells into a crowded segment of established vendors and remains small, active and unexited.
notes: Pre-seed confirmed by HIT Consultant and the HLTH syndication (search listing), also a newswire release. Other totals (PitchBook 2.3M, Tracxn about 4M) unverified. Competitor names come from Adentris's own undated comparison, so the dated list is left empty. Sergey and Alex backgrounds come only from the YC page.
